theme.title: The Numbers Game
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: What was Steve Nash's assists-per-game average for the 2004–05 Suns?
questions.note: 11.5 assists each night in his first MVP season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Nash finished the season averaging 11.5 assists per game

funFacts.text: Nash shot 50.2% from the field and 43.1% from three during the regular season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: while making 50.2% of his field goals and 43.1% of his three-pointers

funFacts.text: Nash won MVP while Mike D'Antoni took Coach of the Year and Bryan Colangelo Executive of the Year.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He ended up winning the MVP award. D'Antoni was awarded Coach of the Year

funFacts.text: Quentin Richardson won the Three-Point Shootout during the same season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Quentin Richardson won the Three-Point Shootout

questions.prompt: The 2011–12 Bobcats lost 23 straight. A year before their title, how long was the 2006–07 Celtics' franchise-record losing streak?

funFacts.text: Second-year point guard Rajon Rondo started alongside Boston's newly formed Big Three.

funFacts.text: Boston had not reached the Finals since the Bird-era rivalry with the Lakers.

questions.prompt: How many points per game did Reggie Miller average in 1997–98?

funFacts.text: Miller scored 1,578 points during the regular season.
He spent 34.5 minutes per game on the floor.
Miller scored a team-high 28 in a 107–105 win over Chicago on May 23, 1998.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: May 23, 1998 Chicago W 107–105 Miller (28)

questions.prompt: Before the famous 2016 Finals Game 7, the Cavs and Warriors had the same total points through six games. How many each?
questions.context: Cleveland vs Golden State · 2016 Finals · through Game 6
questions.note: 610 each. The 2016 Finals were perfectly even in total points before Cleveland's historic Game 7 win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: both teams entered Game 7 with the same total points scored through six games (610 points each)

funFacts.text: Cleveland edged Golden State in the decider, 93–89.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Cavaliers defeated the Warriors 93–89 in Game 7

funFacts.text: The decider featured 20 lead changes and 11 ties.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The game was close, with 20 lead changes and 11 ties.

funFacts.text: LeBron's legendary chase-down block preserved an 89-all tie.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: LeBron James delivered what became known as "The Block" on a layup attempt by Andre Iguodala with the score tied at 89
